summary: All six round-1 findings (S1-S6) are fixed in the committed plan. S1: active OST capacity now grows with N. Each stream gets N*s0 stripes over N*P1 distinct OSTs, with a 128-stripe cap, OST/OSS inventory, overlap rejection, a check that the expanded layout is actually exercised, and the same files for replay and application (test-plan.md:223-249). S2: B_pattern is exact descriptor replay with its own concurrency plateau. Coalesced replay is diagnostic only, and a lower-bound reference withholds the saturation claim (15-26, Phase C at 161). S3: the cold-read check needs OSC/RPC or other validated wire-level counters. llite is application-level only, and expected bytes = bigdata + a readahead allowance fixed in preflight + SMD, with SMD kept out of the numerator (131-146). S4: a D_node-sized corpus is required before sustained Phases B-E, and short pilot runs cannot pass the plateau or saturation gates (166-170). S5: confidence intervals use a Student-t interval on paired log-ratios, fixed in advance, with at least five independent blocks, a leave-one-block-out check and an 'inconclusive' outcome (292-301). S6: PS_EB_NODE_LOCAL is a separately costed topology with its own N=1 reference, and cache-residency checks cover every range a node could be sent under dynamic scheduling (120-124, 205-210). I found no regressions. The baseline SHA is unchanged in test-plan.md and baseline.json. The plan does not claim any current measurement. Host, staging and calibration stay separate. Quota math still holds: 11.52 TB at 20 GB/s fits in the roughly 16.4 TB left after 20% headroom and existing use, and the plan correctly says 40 GB/s does not fit. One new non-blocking clarification (S7): it is not specified which layout the paired one-worker weak-scaling reference B_1 reads. This is document-level approval only. No runtime test, benchmark, staging or job has run.

findings.evidence: E(N)=B(N)/(N*B(1)) (line 43). Each N uses its own layout with N*s0 stripes over N*P1 OSTs (lines 223-231). Weak-scaling blocks pair the N-node rate with 'a one-worker reference on the same allocation' (303-306), but nothing says which layout that reference reads. If it reads the N=1 layout (s0 stripes over P1 OSTs), the reference layout must also be staged next to the N layout, which strains 'stage one large layout at a time' (264). If it reads a 1/N slice of the N layout, the reference touches up to N*P1 OSTs and B_1 can differ from the N=1 series point. The two readings give different E(N) values, and results could mix them across N.
findings.requested_change: Choose and record one B_1 definition per series. Recommended: a one-worker run on the frozen N=1 layout, staged alongside each N layout and counted in the quota budget. Optionally also report the 1/N-slice-of-N-layout reference as a labeled diagnostic. Record the reference layout hash in every weak-scaling block.
